problem: writeExportFile swallows every mkdir/writeFile failure (it logs only when KERYX_VERBOSE is set) and returns normally. Its only caller, runHistoryExport, then prints `exported N run(s) to <file>` and leaves exitCode 0. Error-handling Rule 3 / Iron Law 1: a catch that hides a failure from a caller who then proceeds. Class scope: this is the only write site in the new file (writeExportFile is called once, at line 122).
impact: A user exporting to an unwritable path (read-only dir, path under an existing file, full disk) is told the export succeeded with exit 0. No file exists, and scripts or flow journals that attach the export break later with no clue why.

problem: The doc comment on collectRunRows is stale. It says the function returns runs oldest first, 'so the exported file reads in the order the writes happened'. In fact it only filters the output of listWikiRuns, which sorts newest first (src/wiki/history.ts:495 `Runs newest first` and line 508 sorts descending). No reversal is done anywhere.
impact: Readers and callers take the documented ordering on trust. The exported file is in reverse of the order the comment promises, and the next person to 'fix' the order may first have to find out which of the two is right.
quote:
Returns the runs
 * oldest first, so the exported file reads in the order the writes happened.

problem: The command-label normalisation chain (collapse newlines, collapse whitespace, trim, clip to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH) is copied three times: twice inside renderRunLine (lines 49-53 and 56-60) and once in src/commands/wiki-history.ts:47-51. Only MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH is shared. The pure transform is not.
impact: Anyone changing how labels are clipped or cleaned has to edit three copies in two files and keep them in step. The terminal list and the two export formats drift as soon as one copy is missed.

problem: renderRunLine takes a boolean flag `markdown` that switches between two separate renderers (markdown row vs CSV row), and it has 4 positional parameters. Two of those parameters (`at`, `pages`) are fields of the `run` it already receives. The call site reads `renderRunLine(run, at, run.pages, format === "md")`. This crosses both the boolean-flag threshold and the >=4 positional-parameter threshold in solid-principles.mdc.
impact: Call sites cannot be read without opening the signature. Adding a third format means growing the flag into a branch. The redundant `pages`/`at` arguments also let a caller pass values that disagree with `run`.

problem: collectRunRows catches the listWikiRuns failure and rethrows a new Error without `{ cause: error }`. The bound `error` is unused, and the message drops the input (the runs log path or cwd). This breaks error-handling Rule 5 / Iron Law 3 and Rule 2.
impact: When the runs log cannot be read (permission, corrupt filesystem), the original errno and stack are lost. The user and whoever debugs it get only 'could not read the runs log', with no path and no reason.
quote: throw new Error("wiki history: could not read the runs log");

problem: runHistoryExport is about 57 lines and does several separable jobs at different levels: argv validation, format inference from the extension, date parsing and normalisation of --since, row rendering, the file write, and realpath-based display. The --format and --since parsing blocks are self-contained pure parsers that could be helpers returning a value or an error message.
impact: The parsing rules (format inference, date normalisation) can only be tested by driving the whole command through the filesystem. Each new flag lengthens one function that already mixes orchestration with low-level string handling.

problem: There are three usage strings for the export command, and they no longer agree. HISTORY_USAGE omits --since and --command. EXPORT_USAGE (wiki-history-export.ts:13) and the help text in src/commands/wiki.ts:924 list them.
impact: A user who sees the HISTORY_USAGE error gets an incomplete description of the flags. Keeping three hand-written copies in sync is a maintenance cost each time a flag is added.
quote: "Usage: keryx wiki history <page> | keryx wiki history --runs [--json] [--export <file> [--format csv|md]]";

problem: The guard `target.startsWith("--")` repeats a check that optionValue already makes: src/lib/args.ts:24 returns undefined when the next token is a flag. In the space-separated form the branch cannot be reached. It only matters for `--export=--x`, which the guard silently treats as missing.
impact: It is dead-looking defensive code with no comment saying which spelling it is for, so a reader cannot tell whether removing it is safe.
